text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Compared to a similar camera made by Belkin, setting up the D-Link was kind of a pain. Not as much of a pain as setting up a Foscam F18918W - where you get directed to a third party domain name provider and get to learn the joys of port forwarding - but a relative hassle.

For the Belkin, I opened the box, plugged into my router, ran a set up program that took less than five minutes, downloaded an app, and I was up and running. While this is a very similar product in both look and function, it took over an hour - and two ethernet cables - to set it up. There is no Mac software on the installation cd. The box states that a Windows pc is required, but the website has a Mac download available. You have to scroll through the product photos, which aren't in alphanumeric order. Just keep looking until you find the DCS-930L - AFTER the 931L and the 932L and the 934L. Have faith. Keep going. It's there.

Once you get the program installed, it takes very little time to *find* the camera and teach it to log into your wireless network. And then you are back to the website to set up your account and view your camera. Except you are on a Mac, and the viewer requires you to install the Java Runtime Environment. JRE is a big old security vulnerability on Macs. So much so that Apple advises against using it. Mavericks lets you turn it on case by case - and, by default, it will ask you every time before running it. If you are on an OS below Mavericks, check the googles for setting your preferences so that you're not running JRE all the time.

Okay, so now you've got JRE going, and the first thing the program tells you is that you have to update your firmware AND you need to have the camera AND your computer ethernet-jacked right into your router. LOLWUT? I'm lucky. I am on a laptop, and I have an extra ethernet cable and an empty port. So, I did that, and there I was, up and running, about an hour, hour and a half, thereabouts, after I started.

Image quality is pretty good - not great. Audio is okay. The settings are very customizable. But the wifi receiver is very weak, and that limits the usefulness of this product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th) I got the HD 8 as a replacement to my old Kindle keyboard that died on a camp trip. I had such high hopes this device would fit the bill. I am not going to go into the nitty gritty of pros and cons but will sum up my experience highlights.

- the Audio performance is amazing. It is a quantum improvement from the audio I get on my iPad Mini. The sound experience is really something Apple should strive for. It did knock my socks off.

- setup was easy and efficient, but I think the OS and maybe even the device has problems. I have had to call tech support about twice a day on days I use the device. It is usually a lockup or hang or feature that does not work. I think I have isolated the problem to the fact the device can't keep the OS stable on battery. They always have me plug the device into the adapter for any support call (regardless of its charge level) and it always starts behaving itself once it is on DC power vs battery. I have also seen it burn through battery pretty fast at times. Not sure what it is doing but it ate 10% sitting on standby in my pack on the commute to work this morning!

- I do think the read aloud smarts have been improved since the older model (kbd) as it reads much cleaner now for me. (Less stops, more in the right locations, etc).

My end-game is that I will probably return it. If it does not work reliably on battery then it is not a mobile device. Period.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 8 Tablet, 8" HD Display, Wi-Fi, 8 GB - Includes Special Offers, Magenta (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G) I got this for Christmas and have only been using it for a few days now. I did have a problem with the set-up since there were no step by step instructions and you are left to figure out what goes where. I had omitted attaching the USB/phone jack between my old Windows XP computer and the UPS. I've used UPS's in years past, but they did not require a USB connection to a computer. I found out I had a problem when I was trying to install the software and it stopped loading and gave me a problem message, but no solution. I called the 1-888 number and without any fuss or waiting I got to speak to someone in the tech department who spoke very good English and solved my problem quickly.

I was tempted to deduct one star for the lousy (or total lack of) any instructions on how to connect this to your computer but didn't since the tech help was so good. There was a picture drawing instructing the user to remove the battery and turn it over so the green tape is on top which I managed to do alright. I don't hear any fan noise whatsoever as some others were complaining of. In fact, it's so quiet I can't even tell it's on unless I go and see the 3 LED lights on the top panel.

I tested it out a few minutes ago by turning off the power to the room that my computer is in. I was downstairs in the garage at the fuse box so I don't know if any beep occurred upstairs, but when I got there the computer was running off the UPS. Every 30 seconds I heard 4 beeps from the UPS telling me that it was being used as the power source. I only have my computer, monitor and modem connected to the UPS. I figure I don't need the extra peripheral equipment to stay powered up since it only sucks more energy from my UPS. I didn't wait to see how long the UPS would power my PC but I did sit there for about 3 minutes before I went downstairs and turned the power back on. My computer had a message on the screen saying that it was now being powered by regular current again (or something to that effect).

So far I like this UPS a LOT. There's nothing more frustrating then losing your work if the power goes off for only a couple of seconds. I edit a lot of music and it's not always easy or convenient to save it while I edit it just because of the nature of the program I use. So, I really like the idea of hearing my 4 beeps to let me know I might need to close out and shut down and not lose any work. I don't always have lights on so there may be nothing to tell me there's been a power outage except for the beeps on this UPS. There is a mute mode, but I need to hear the beeps.
text_fidelity_b: APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G)

Bose QuietComfort Noise Cancelling Earbuds-Bluetooth Wireless Earphones, Triple Black My family has tested out numerous noise canceling earbuds in the last six months, looking for the best ones to fit each member of our household. This set of earbuds was the universal favorite among every member of our family.

For one, the noise cancellation feature is absolutely the most effective noise cancellation we have found on earbuds. Even having it on silent, I was unable to discern individual words from my mom reading loudly to my two noisy children in the other room. With an audiobook playing, I really didn't notice anybody else being in the house, though I could hear them if I thought about it. With music, it was like they weren't there, someone can stand right next to me and talk to me and I can be blissfully unaware.

If you get overloaded from auditory stimulation easily and just need the world to stop making so much noise every so often, these are the earbuds to get.

The sound quality is extraordinarily good on audiobooks, rap music, metal music, and more peaceful and soothing ballads and classical. The base was not overwhelming, nor did the treble get screechy.

It fit my very small ears well, and fit my husband's ears well also, he has a much bigger ear canal size.

The one thing that we have both noticed is that these are also heavier than most of our other earbuds, however even with my ears feeling rather sensitive, it really didn't bother me because they are weighted nicely and fit so well.

Overall, while these could be improved by being slightly smaller and less heavy, these still beat out five other well-known brands in our household for both the noise cancellation and in audio quality.

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier I've had problems with Pixmas in the past, mostly having to do with wireless networks and having to reinstall the software over and over to try to get them to hang on to network settings. I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

Quite impressed.

MS video viewer downloads. plays and files as usual. Haven't needed any software to get this far ... which is as far as I need it.

text_fidelity_a: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black ) This is a great, little device!  First of all, I think it's beautiful and sleek, and easy to use.  Just slide it open, plug in the cable that links to your iPod, and if you are using batteries, that's it, good to go.  Just plug in the AC cord if you aren't using batteries.  Uses 4 AAA batteries, so the batteries are small, don't add any noticeable weight to the unit.  Your iPod stays in it's own protective case, no fitting it onto a dock slot.  I've had one Altec Lansing speaker set and one Sonic Impact speaker set that the slot became damaged, so I'm glad I don't deal with that anymore.  This thing is light, small, about the size of a very, VERY large eyeglasses case so it packs very nicely in a purse, carry-on or suitcase, even better if you can get along without the bulky AC cord and just use batteries.  But it's about the sound, isn't it?  If you are looking for sound in your hotel room, or bathroom, mobile home, bedroom, kitchen, garage, den, etc., you are going to LOVE this little guy, and it will be more than loud enough, it can crank!  The sound is really great!  It looks great, performs great, and I just bought another one for a friend going to Mexico in a week.  Now, if you want a loud, space-filling but still portable speaker, get the In-Motion IM9 unit, as I did also.  I have both.  The IM9 is too big for the suitcase, and it's REALLY heavy, but it's screaming loud, great for the backyard or tailgating or any party setting, and very compact and portable while protecting the iPod within it's great loading system.  But this JBL is your OTHER speaker system for light weight travel or just to fill a room at home.  If you don't love it as I do, I don't know what planet you live on!
text_fidelity_b: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black )

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker Beyond the way it looks, it's relatively easy to pair via Bluetooth, you can charge your phone via USB or NFC, the wireless near-field connection scheme. I'd have given a tooth for an external speaker like this back in the 80s, when battery-powered speakers for the Sony Walkman existed. It's more than adequate for a dorm room or office space, it's lightweight, it seems to be pretty durable, each of the EIGHT speakers have a metal screen protecting the cones. CX -- No, I was wrong, there are NOT eight speakers, there are FOUR speakers, plus four extra cones which amplify the sound. I counted the grilles and assumed they were all speakers. My error!

This comes in a beautiful package, it would make a fantastic gift. It promises up to 8-10 hours of play, which is more than decent. There's a Mic In jack, which I'm somewhat baffled by, and an Aux jack, which is very handy if you own an older non-Bluetooth iPod. There's a Talk button for use with your phone. I'm unclear how that would function. This can be mounted on a wall, AND THEY INCLUDED THE WALL ANCHORS AND SCREWS. Very thoughtful.

The main thing, the sound quality, is better than I've heard with other Bluetooth speaker solutions, which, honestly, is not saying that much. I'm looking for a software EQ on my iPhone and I don't find one. I don't want to ask for the Moon, but an EQ on the speaker would be worth more to me than the NFC charging scheme.

A very good Bluetooth speaker solution. It looks gorgeous, it's easily paired, the sound is relatively bright and clear. Room-filling sound. It won't replace home stereos, but that's not what it's meant to do. Anyone young enough to NOT remember how good vinyl LPs sound will be positively thrilled with this device!

---

This device actually sounds better filling a room with sound than it does just sitting on your desk. For whatever that's worth. It sounds better if it's not right under your nose.

---

This device does match up with my iPhone very well, and without a lot of fuss or headaches like other Bluetooth solutions I've tried. If I can't get each device to sniff one another's butt, I lose interest pretty quickly. This device matches up on its own and easily, so that's a major plus.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver) I've been thinking about upgrading from my Canon 50d for awhile now. I thought I wanted a full frame camera, but I could never justify spending that kind of money on a hobby. One of the main reasons was that I had sort of got out of the habit of shooting as much as I used. Part of the reason was that it always seemed like such a pain to lug around the camera. There were always times I wish I had a camera, but didn't.

This camera solves a lot of that for me. Take the lens off the body and the thing literally fits in your pocket. Leave it on and it fits nicely in my car's center console. It feels nice in my hands, although I bought the metal thumb grip at the same time as the camera and must admit that does help quite a bit.

Compared to my 50d (which is a little long in the tooth) the image quality is superior. The color reproduction in particular seemed to be good. It also seemed to perform better at higher ISOs than my 50d does. Really, the only area where the 50d still out-performs the XE-2 is how fast the autofocus works. The XE-2 is good, but my 50d is still a touch better. Maybe a firmware update will improve this.

Despite using a Canon products for almost a decade, I found I really like the controls on this camera. I found it really easy and intuitive to change the shutter speed and aperature. ISO and most of the other frequently used settings are easily reached by hitting the Q button. The layout could be tweaked a little, but overall it's pretty good.

I've never had a camera with wifi, but it's a feature that's gotten more use than I thought it would. Being able to transmit pictures to Facebook, Twitter, or whatever is really simple once you upload the photo from the camera using Fuji's app. I don't post a lot of pictures online, but that may change a little bit now that it is a lot simpler.

The build quality is really good and the included kit lens is really nice. The screen is sharp and the EVF is clear. Like I mentioned before, the size of the frame is nice and compact and is much easier to take along wherever you go.

Is this a replacement for a full frame DSLR? No. Is it a good alternative for a crop sensor DSLR? In my opinion, absolutely. First, the price and performance makes it very competitive. Second, the size is going to be tough to beat. Finally, for me at least, it is a camera I am more likely to use more and take with me more places. As other's have mentioned about this camera though, if you like putting everything on automatic or different shooting modes (sports, portrait, landscape, etc) then this camera is probably not for you. If you are interested in learning how to shoot without those crutches, this camera would be a great place to start.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm X-E2 16.3 MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3.0-Inch LCD - Body Only (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Elite Active 75t True Wireless Bluetooth, Navy – Earbuds for Running and Sport, Charging Case Included, 24 Hour Battery, Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds Pros--
-Very comfortable and secure fit even during high intensity exercise
-Solid Bluetooth connection
-Good noise canceling
-Hear thru mode is useful
-Sleek, low profile look
-Decent battery life, charging case is nice
-mic works well for calls or voice commands
-LOTS of bass (I consider this a major negative, but some people will like the bass heavy sound)

CONS-
-Below average sound quality (WAY too much bass, even after using the EQ to turn down the bass its still more than I would prefer for most types of music, the default out of the box sound is the worst I have ever heard on a pair of headphones in this price range.. but that said you can make them sound pretty decent after a bit of tweaking with the EQ)
-Not loud enough, the maximum volume is barely adequate for high external noise situations like airplane (even with the noise cancellation which works pretty well)
-Sealed design is not good for 'active' pursuits because of microphonic effect amplifying internal sounds whenever you move around
-software can be buggy, occasionally when I change settings and they appear to be changed in the software but do not apply to the buds

I think there are certain people who will love these buds, especially if you listen to a lot of rap/hiphop or other bass heavy music as the default sound seems to be tuned for that kind of music. Personally I just can't really get into the sound of these, even after tweaking with the EQ there is too much bass and the soundstage is flat and lifeless. I do like a lot of things about them though, the fit is comfortable and very secure, much better than airpods or galaxy buds on that front.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Elite Active 75t True Wireless Bluetooth, Navy – Earbuds for Running and Sport, Charging Case Included, 24 Hour Battery, Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II Mirrorless Camera with 14-42mm II R Lens (Black) I wanted an ILM camera I could use with low f-stop manual lenses. I have some nice old f/1.9 & f/2.8 MC Rokkor lenses from 45 years ago.
My Lumix ZS70 is great for everything but low light & a few specialized uses. For those you need interchangeable lenses.
This package with two kit lenses is roughly the equivalent of my ZS70. Both lenses work fine. I'm still learning the menus & controls. It handles well on my monopod.
Edit:
I bought an inexpensive Fotasy adapter for the Minolta lenses. It works fine. The camera switches to full manual mode automatically. I did take some online advice & set up two of the programmable buttons for peaking & magnification to help with manual focusing. The resulting shutter speeds are nice, up to 8 times faster.
Edit:
This is a small camera, only a little larger than a P&S. That's normally good. Except when the temperatures are in the teens (F). Even thin leather driving gloves are a bit clumsy, especially with the back panel buttons. I normally use fingerless mittens, but not this morning.
Edit:
I'm really liking this camera. My lens changing/handling skills are coming back after not being used for [cough] years. In terms of focal lengths, the basic kit lens (14-42mm) is good for 80% of shots. I'd wish for a couple of more f-stops, though.
Edit, 5/16/2020
Longer term: Still good. I have the F3 button set on MF. There are a few cases where the AF algorithm & I disagree. For some reason, buttercup yellow flowers have no inherent contrast & AF has a hard time seeing the details to focus. This brings up peaking & magnify & allows me to fine tune the focus.
I keep wishing for a 20-80 mm f/2.8 lens. Cheap, of course. ;)
text_fidelity_b: Olympus OM-D E-M10 Mark II Mirrorless Camera with 14-42mm II R Lens (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link N300 Wireless Portable Nano Travel Router(TL-WR802N) - WiFi Bridge/Range Extender/Access Point/Client Modes, Mobile in Pocket I purchased this to try and create my own wireless network within a hospital room I would be in for a while. The problem as many have stated is most commercial WiFi system require you log into a splash page after you connect to their network. This router does not have a way to do that. You can try using one of your devices and then clone the MAC address to the router, but this only works if this router is connected to the network with the Ethernet cable port. Most hotels and hospitals no longer have working Ethernet jacks in rooms. If you try and clone the MAC address on the wireless port it creates a conflict and everything stops working.

So to sum up, it works fine as a cheap travel router, but if you have to deal with a splash page on an WiFi only network, it simply will not work. It can’t be that hard to create one of these with a built in browser for splash pages. Anyone listening????
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link N300 Wireless Portable Nano Travel Router(TL-WR802N) - WiFi Bridge/Range Extender/Access Point/Client Modes, Mobile in Pocket

As a side note, don't skimp on your sub, a great sub can make a HUGE difference for all the speakers in your home theater.

I bought one pair for my front L & R and I was so impressed that I bought another to use as my center channel (they only come in pairs so I have an extra speaker in case I blow one out!). I replaced my Martin Logan center with this (laid on its side) and it handles dialog better. Now all 3 speakers in my front soundstage are these Sonys and my system has never sounded better.

I am not a fan of the grills, the Sony logo looks a bit cheap, so I use them without the grills and they look great.

I don't think these would be great for music, that "warmth" that people love for playing music usually distorts dialog. I only occasionally listen to music on my system and I think they are fine but I wanted to mention that because it might be an issue for some people. These are clear as a bell, keep that in mind.

Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black Before you buy, check the Monoprice website for this item. The price may be much cheaper over there.

This is a very inexpensive, relatively low quality TV antenna. You get what you pay for. They advertise this for both indoor and outdoor use, but the mostly plastic construction will not last long outdoors in areas that get a lot of wind, ice, or bright sunlight. The attached 3 foot cable really tells you what their intended use case is. If your TV is near a window, hang the antenna in the window, plug it in, and you're done.

The advertised 50 mile range is for ideal conditions, mounting the antenna outdoors in an area where there are absolutely no obstructions between your home and the TV broadcast tower (no trees, no buildings, etc). Expect much worse range for an indoor mounting and if there are any obstructions. If you live in an area with trees etc, you should get a more sturdy antenna that can be mounted on a pole on top of your roof so it can receive a signal over the trees.

This antenna is advertised for UHF frequencies only. Most TV stations use UHF these days, but in my area there are a couple that use VHF and this antenna is not usable for those channels. If you really want VHF, I suggest getting a different antenna from this one.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Active Indoor/Outdoor HD6 HDTV Antenna, 50 Mile Range, Video Antenna (115953) Black

The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

I normally use a 7D Mk ii with various telephoto prime and telephoto zooms for wildlife photography and 5D Mk iv with wide angle prime and zooms for landscape shots. I recently had to go on a trip where it was impossible to bring any of my DSLR kits due to space and weight limitations. I was able get a super deal on a Panasonic FZ-1000 (I guess this is quite an older model at this time). I was somewhat skeptical about the specs at first, but the Leica lens and the 1" sensor performed really well on my test shots, so I decided to take the FZ-1000 as my camera for the trip. The results were surprisingly good. The camera has quick and intuitive user interface, good set of manual controls and several programmable function buttons, so it is relatively easy to learn and set it up to one's preferences. The AF system certainly exceeded my expectations. It did an excellent job of picking subjects behind branches/partial foliage. The success rate for birds in flight was quite good, not nearly as fast or accurate as a 7D Mk ii with EF 400 f/5.6L, but good enough for all practical purposes. Exposure both in scene mode and spot mode (a somewhat large spot) was good. Battery life was also very good. I was getting more than 600 shots per charge using the optical viewfinder and no flash. I did not try the 4K video feature yet, but the 1080p video quality was also very good. The whole package is as big as a low-end DSLR with a kit lens, but gives you 25mm-400mm effective focal range, a relatively fast lens (f/4.0 even at 400mm) plenty of manual control, and a very good AE/AF system. Highly recommended for travel when there is space/weight limitations.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic LUMIX FZ1000 II 20.1MP Digital Camera, 16x 25-400mm LEICA DC Lens, 4K Video, Optical Image Stabilizer and 3.0-inch Display – Point and Shoot Camera - DC-FZ1000M2 (Black)

SABRENT 7 Port USB 3.0 HUB + 2 Charging Ports with 12V/4A Power Adapter [Black] (HB-U930) This is a nicely design USB hub. It has the two feature I look for first in a hub: a compact footprint, and the ability to plug into the wall without having to deal with a wall wart at the end of the plug. While this does have a transformer, it is an in-line version that doesn't interfere with the plug end.

Installation is the typical plug-and-play that is typical with a USB hub. It includes a USB 3.0 cable, and works very well as a USB 3.0 hub under Win 7. I also tried it on an older USB 2.0 machine running XP and had no problems at all (running, of course, at USB 2.0 speed).

The build quality feels very solid. No problems with ports wiggling around even when I stressed the USB cable far more than in normal use. I’ve used other Sabrent hubs and have yet to have a problem with them, even after dropping them.

The hub includes a base that keeps it well-planted in use.

In addition to using this as a USB hub, it also has 2 charging ports that provide 2A output each. Both worked fine when used to charge a phone and a tablet.

The only quibble I have is that it lacks an on/off switch. Not a big deal, but having a switch can come in handy at times.

Overall, it’s a well-designed and well-built hub with a number of good design features. Well worth considering if you’re looking for a compact 3.0 hub with a lot of ports.
[Sample provided for review]

OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK So. Yes. It’s sturdy and seems it’ll protect an iPad really well.

Unfortunately, for the past 6 years, we’ve been spoiled by an iPad mini case made by Ballistic, that isn’t made any more. So I just don’t buy “well sure it’s inconvenient and bulky but it has to be, to protect well.” It really does not.

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.

My home is just over 3000 sq ft. and this router provides great signal strength throughout the whole house without any additional mesh nodes. Note that my house is 3 stories though and the router is centrally located on the middle floor. If your house is more spread out then additional nodes may be required to cover 3000 sq ft adequately.

Hardware wise this router seems great, the software is a bit klunky though compared to my previous ASUS router. Also its extremely annoying that they try to force you to use their phone app to set up the router. text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) My top ten include dogs, sewing machines, houses, my bed, a few trips, and my Kindle. I love my Kindle so much that I actually bought a Kindle edition of a big, heavy, expensive book that I have in hardback just so I don't have to carry it around. It has taken just one month for me to only want to read with the Kindle. It's going to save lots of bookshelf space, my bookshelves are jammed. I love being able to use the dictionary and look up many more words than I used to. Yes, you know the meaning from the context, but it's fun to know the etymology. I took Latin many years ago and frequently consider the root meanings of words, and having the Kindle dictionary makes this easier. Wikipedia is wonderful, too. I looked up the Magna Charta while I was reading a book that mentioned it, and found when it was written, what it was about, etc. I have also looked up some cities to find demographic and weather information.
The ability to change font size and page justification is a good feature. It is important to realize, however, that you can't change justification if the book wasn't formatted to allow that. You get those giant gaps on some lines when it's in full justification. If you use a small font, it's not so bad. Most of the books I have purchased allow left justification, and my guess is that more and more books will be formatted that way, which generally eliminates those gaps. You can get the first chapters of books as free samples, and see how they are formatted, as well as whether you like them as far as writing and subject is concerned.
The next thing I plan to do is put some of my music from my iPod onto the Kindle so I can listen to background music while I read. I understand you can't control the order of the songs, so I'm only going to put on classical music that is not distracting in and of itself.
Getting more books fast is great, too. I forget the name for the phobia that is the fear of running out of things to read, but I have a small case of that, and Kindle is the cure.
Traveling is much nicer when you don't have ten books in your book bag.
I'm asking for an SD card for Christmas from one of the grandkids (it's very inexpensive) so that the Kindle will have even greater capacity.
When you go to the Kindle store from your Kindle, there will be recommendations based on what you have bought, just like there are when you go to Amazon online. However, online you can say "not interested," but on the Kindle, you can't. You get the same recommendations over and over. It would be nice if you could delete recommendations from your Kindle. But, hey, that is definitely just a small thing.
Another thing that would be nice is a password for 1-click ordering from the Kindle.
I'm retired and on a relatively small income. If I lost my Kindle and couldn't afford another one, I would go back to work just long enough to get the money to replace it. That should tell you how much I love it, 'cause I sure don't want to work anymore!
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
ECHOGEAR Swivel TV Stand - Universal Replacement Stand for TVs Up to 60"- Height Adjustable Up to 4" & Smooth TV Swivel - Works with Samsung, LG, Sony & More I got a new 50 inch 7 series samsung tv that has a curved back, so the screws that came with the stand does not fit. The required screws were M8 x 45mm, but the longest screws were m8 x 35mm. I'm ok with that as this screen is newer and has a different curve on teh back than most flatscreen tvs out there.

After a run to Fastenal to obtain the right length screws, everything installed fine. In order to level horizontal axis properly, I left the screws on the horizontal bar slightly loose. After putting on the screen, adjust for horizontal level, and then tighten the screws on the horizontal bar.

Only issue that i came into after that was the whole tv would lean backwards ever so slightly, like 4-5 degrees. Very noticeable since my tv is next to a door and bookcase. I noticed the problem was in the design of the vertical bars that are installed onto the tv itself.

The upper hook part that clips onto the top part of the horizontal bar is not the same thickness as the bottom hook part that sits on the lower part of the horizontal bar. Thin vertical top, thicker vertical bottom, you get a screen that is angled looking slightly up. Maybe its a design flaw or maybe its designed to accommodate heavier TV's that may cause the screen to lean forward (my tv was kinda light).

A fix for my TV leaning back was shoving a few shims under the back of the base plate to get it to lean more forward (i used a stack of like 8 business cards on both rear corners of the base plate; seems to work fine).

Overall, i'm happy with my product. The ability to swivel was the sole reason i bought this.
text_fidelity_b: ECHOGEAR Swivel TV Stand - Universal Replacement Stand for TVs Up to 60"- Height Adjustable Up to 4" & Smooth TV Swivel - Works with Samsung, LG, Sony & More

Today my external hard drive is not recognized when it is plugged into this hub. I am NOT restarting my computer to test whether it is necessary to have the HDD recognized. It IS recognized when it is plugged into a different hub that is also plugged into my Mac mini.

Other drives (SSD and HDD) that were connected to this hub also disconnected themselves. The wired Apple aluminum keyboard (it came with my 2008 Mac Pro) is plugged into this hub, and it does not generate the warning that the device was disconnected. If I were shopping for a USB hub, I would stay away from this one. Nothing is "deluxe" except the name - and the lighted ports.

UPDATE (2/9/2019):
My devices - SSDs and 4-bay HDD enclosure - that are plugged into this hub have been disconnecting for no apparent reason. I thought my Logitech mouse was disconnecting because the dongle was plugged into it, but that seems to be the fault of the dongle since it continued while plugged into my keyboard. Connected this to my computer's USB 3.0 port. Plugged in the dongle for my battery powered mouse. Mouse began acting erratically, had to remove the dongle and reinsert it to reconnect. Functioned properly for a short while but disconnected.
Finally had to plug dongle in the port on my wired keyboard before it would stay connected and not perform erratically. Something must be interrupting the signal even when the LEDs indicate the hub is connected even during periods when my computer is asleep.

The hub has 3 smart charging ports, but when viewed from an angle, only the two on the end have orange / red LED light showing - the 3rd one appears blue. All lights are bright - brighter than they need to be.

A 4-bay HDD enclosure is plugged into this hub and has been functioning without any problem for the 2 weeks I have had the enclosure connected. Connecting an SSD through this hub also functions with no problem using a SATA-USB3 cable.

Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer) These are perhaps the best in ear earphones I've ever used. They are lightweight, comfortable, stay in your ear, and offer great sound.

I've long ago ditched most earbud style earphones. They offer horrible sound, are uncomfortable, and never stay in your ear. These earphones address those issues with style, comfort, and great sound reproduction.

The mid and high range reproduction is crisp and clean without any noticeable distortion. Low range is somewhat lacking but is proberly above what most small earbud style headphones are.

They feature many great design features such as replaceable buds for the earpiece. There is small, medium, and large. There is also a set of memory foam that you can choose. This is good because as everyone's ears are different, most earpieces are not. This allows you to choose the fit of the earbuds to suit your own needs.

The part of the cable that plugs into your walkman, diskman, iPod or whatever is steel reinforced, which is nice as that is what usually breaks first on headphones. They also come with a steel carrying case to protect your headphones when not in use. They also have a cleaning tool to clean any nasty bits that may get into the canal of the phones.

All-in-all a great set of phones for the audiophile. They are lightweight, sound great, and most importantly, stay in your ear and are comfortable.

I bought this because the Mac Pro doesn't have an internal mic. Amazingly it also doesn't have a mic port. It has 3.5 mm headphones and speaker ports. I thought I could plug this into one of those ports. No luck.
The headset port apparently requires a 4 conductor 3.5 mm TRRS plug. Neither the computer maker nor the mic/headset maker ever give you this type of critical information. I probably should have purchased a USB mic instead. So now I either buy a USB mic or a USB adaptor.

My general comment about microphones and headsets is that the descriptions (both Amazons and the manufacturers) are almost always weak on connectors, adaptors and compatability (PC/MAC/etc). This is the most important feature and should be at the top of any description. After all if it doesn't fit or work what good is it.

Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This is a retro leather laptop messenger bag - the material is made from something called "Buffalo" leather, which feels rough and stiff - quite the opposite of lambskin or buttery soft leather. The buckles are only for show because you can open and close the bag without unbuckling it, as there are buttons underneath. It has a weathered look, with varying shades of brown and sienna that give the impression that you're an Indiana Jones-type adventurer who's been carrying this bag through the outback, escaped tigers and bears, and came through fine, though the bag is a bit battered.

In other words, it's very manly, and harks back to the 1940s when bulky items were the norm because thinner materials hadn't been invented yet. While it looks great and seems well made (it's from India), it's actually limited in terms of actual everyday use. If you're traveling a lot, you want things to be as lightweight as possible. This is not one of those items. Even when empty, it feels cumbersome to carry. Stuffed with a laptop and papers, it will be heavy.

Think about it - when was the last time you actually saw someone on the train or airport carrying one of these? You might say you'd like to do so because it will make you look unique. In reality, other people may have tried carrying one of these and gave up.

So while it's nice as a conversation piece and something you might want to show off to your friends, I fear it will be one of those novelty items that, after its newness has worn off, will be relegated to the back of the closet.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) One of the main reasons I selected this model is the simplicity of a single battery cartridge design. My previous APC UPS units use spade connectors. I have limited use of my hands and fingers which makes it a challenge to use spade connectors so I was looking forward to the cartridge battery simplicity. When the product arrived I installed it as per the clear and easy to follow directions. But the UPS acted as if the battery was not connected and / or missing altogether. After spending a considerable time diagnosing the problem I finally removed the cartridge battery (Aaa-gain) to make a close inspection. I found there are two male blade connectors located within a pocket in the cartridge battery. Two female blade connectors are located in a protrusion inside the UPS unit battery compartment so as to self align and engage the male blades inside the pocket in the cartridge battery when the cartridge battery is installed and seated fully. One of the two male blade connectors is either missing or pressed in too deep to be reached by the mating coupling. I made a feeble attempt to tug at the stubby male blade sunk deep within the socket but gave up when I realized how stupid the situation is. This is a brand new product so why should I attempt to make a risky repair?

The problem as I see it is in attempting to get two flimsy electrical connectors to self align the first time every time all the time. If they had used common banana jacks instead of spade connectors it would only cost a penny more yet be so much more reliable.

As I write this I am awaiting a reply from APC. If APC will not take care of this problem then I will return my purchase to Amazon.com for a refund. I will follow up with the remedy after it is complete.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire 3 A314-23P-R3QA Slim Laptop | 14.0" Full HD IPS Display | AMD Ryzen 5 7520U Quad-Core Processor | AMD Radeon Graphics | 8GB LPDDR5 | 512GB NVMe SSD | Wi-Fi 6 | Windows 11 Home,Silver Pros

1. Very lightweight. It weighs only 4 pounds.
2. Excellent display. It has a full HD screen resolution of 1920x1080. In particular, high resolution digital photos look great on it.
3. Screen size is excellent. It measures a generous 15.6 inches
4. Hard drive is solid state. This makes booting the laptop extremely fast. It is up and running in a mere 30-45 seconds. My previous laptop, which had a mechanical drive, took as much as 10 minutes before it was fully ready to go.
5. Battery charge is good. It lasts up to 7.5 hours.
6. Attractive, modern design. The laptop is slim and sleek, with a lovely, silver color. I especially like the visibility of the backlit keyboard.
7. Excellent price. It offers good value for the cost.

Cons

1. Processing speed is only adequate. Though the speed is probably sufficient for the average user, it could be an issue if you are doing things that require a lot of horsepower, such as editing videos or creating music in digital-audio workstation software.
2. The 4GB of RAM is minimal. This amount of RAM is the very least that any user requires these days. However, it is upgradeable.
3. The hard drive is only 128GB in size. This is a surprisingly small amount for a modern computer. However, it is probably not a problem for the average user.
4. Windows Home "S Mode" may be an issue. It is automatically enabled on the laptop as a security protection for unwary, non-techie users, who might accidentally stray into dangerous territory online that could compromise the laptop. But for the more technically advanced and self-protectively-savvy user, this feature can be very annoying. Fortunately, those same techies can easily figure out how to disable it, which allows the laptop to run the regular Windows Home version.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire 3 A314-23P-R3QA Slim Laptop | 14.0" Full HD IPS Display | AMD Ryzen 5 7520U Quad-Core Processor | AMD Radeon Graphics | 8GB LPDDR5 | 512GB NVMe SSD | Wi-Fi 6 | Windows 11 Home,Silver

The photo quality is expected to be not great since it's already written in the product page, but I'm frustrated to find the thermal paper not working well that it's a kiss or miss. There's different frames to play with, and some frames print better, some you can hardly see, and your object print with the frame...when the frame is clear, you can recognize what your photo is. When your frame disappeared, you hardly recognize what you were seeing. After all, it's really a kid's camera and I felt, if I'm a kid, kidded. For the price point I can get a portable thermal paper printer that print pictures from Bluetooth to your phone. Also one roll came disassembled, was a pain to roll it back together. Hope these information helps you figure out if this is the right product for you. I see this now as a serious kid's camera toy. Also of note that these thermal paper rolls are not sticker. You'll still have to glue pictures on if you want to. They're just regular grocery store receipts quality.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I first became enamored of the garmin company after using the one with a rental car. The ease of use and accuracy was impressive. Unfortunately, that model is no longer in production so I opted for this unit.

In general I am pleased. Easy to set up, the unit features a bright, clear screen. It is a snap to use and the directions have been unfailing accurate. I drive alot and so far have used this unit throughout New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, DC and Virginia. I have had no problem with reception even while traversing mountainous regions. I appreciate the advance notice for turns and the voice command system is a convenience.

However, this unit is not flawless. The robotic voice often mispronounces street names and the voice command system seems a bit hard of hearing when it comes to addresses. I have had to pull over and type in the address. The unit does not like to deviate from its chosen route. For instance, one location I frequent in New York is accessible both by the thruway (toll road) and other non-toll main arteries. Both are about the same distance. When I want to avoid the toll route, the unit will recalculate directing that I turn around and follow the initial route multiple times before adjusting to the alternate route. A big deal, no,but annoying nonetheless. While I have not been terribly plagued by the pop ups, they are annoying and potentially unsafe. While the start up guide and manual are adequate, they are barely so. Whatever happened to detailed instructions? But my biggest gripe is the customer service. I called twice with questions and had ridicualously long waits of fifteen minutes and twenty-five minutes respectively. There is no round the clock service. The last time I called it wasnt even available all week, totally unacceptable.

So while I like this system,there is room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony SRF-M37W Walkman Digital Tuning Weather/FM/AM Stereo Radio (Black) I've had this for a little over a year, and use it while exercising outdoors. It's taken a real beating - dropped it several times, gets wet in the rain/snow, and so on. But, it just keeps on working! Got to love a product that can take a punch.

Reception is pretty good - can pick up several stations quite clearly, and a few more with some static. Sound quality is decent. You won't mistake it for CD-quality, but it's radio, after all. Battery life is very good - goes a few months on an AAA. I just switched to rechargeable batteries, but even with regular alkalines it's pretty cost effective.

The only downside I've encountered was the headphones. Found them to be very uncomfortable, and replaced them very soon after purchasing with a set of ear buds (not sure of the brand - perhaps Sony as well).

It's not as flexible as a MP3 player but I find the radio reception on this to be far better than the reception on my MP3 player that has an FM tuner. Yes, a conventional FM radio is a bit dated, but then again, so am I - sometimes it's nice to just listen to the radio. For the price, this is a great performer.
text_fidelity_b: Sony SRF-M37W Walkman Digital Tuning Weather/FM/AM Stereo Radio (Black)

Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I am a big fan of my kindles. I have the kindle keyboard ereaders 1st and 3rd gen , the 2nd gen Fire 8.9" and last year I bought the 6" Fire. I would not have bought this one except that my 6" Fire has gotten glitchy. I have not had problems with any of my kindles before so I chalked it up to just a bad egg.
I was thinking of replacing it when I found this great deal on the lastest 7" Fire. $100 for a tablet is such a deal. $50 is AMAZING!!
There isn't a huge difference other than this one is a little bigger. It was easy to import everything from my old tablet to my new one. My books, photos, songs, even my book marks from Silk. The set up took minutes.
The home page is different, it looks like the ones on iphones with all the apps on the home page. You can group them into smaller collections, you can also upload your own photo to be the wallpaper. I like this better than the carousel. You can also group your books into collections. There is a button so that you can move between applications without them closing out. It will show all the last places you went so you can pick up where you were and just switch screens. This is my favorite new feature, even more than the change with the home screen.
I'm not super fond of Silk but it is less annoying since they did an upgrade.
I have only had one problem: when I was first setting it up, the screen kept freezing. I rebooted it and I haven't had an issue since.
This is just as fast as my 6" tablet. Battery usage seems the same as well. According to the specs this should be a little slower than the 6" with less battery time but I have not noticed a difference. The plastic back feels only a little less durable than my other kindles but I'm not concerned. I feel like I have gotten quite a deal.
The camera isn't really improved since there isn't a flash and the sound quality is the same as well. Movies look great. I'm really happy that I can add a memory card. Movies, music, and audio books use a lot of memory but now I'll have more memory than I need.
You are getting so much for your money. I've never used other brand tablets, I'm not an Apple user. They may or may not be better but are their prices worth it?
I love Prime access for music and videos and that they can be downloaded.
I'm very happy with my new tablet!
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

Sangean PR-D7 BK AM/FM Digital Rechargeable Portable Radio - Black (PR-D7BK) I like this radio for AM reception. Comes with an AC adapter that also charges the six nickel metal hydride (NiMH) AA cells if you buy and install them. You must throw a little switch (one time process) to tell the radio which type of cells are installed (regular or rechargeable) so the radio doesn't try to recharge the non-rechargeable cells.

One flaw is that it does not have a handle for convenient carrying. It is portable, after all. It's not that you can't carry it, but it's not very "grippable" and a handle is way better. I bought one of these radios for my 90-yr old dad, who was grabbing it by the buttons and accidentally reprogramming it. The handle assures it stays set properly and won't be accidentally dropped.

I epoxied an auxiliary handle on, as you can see in the photo. The handle is simple white plastic door pull left over from a prefab storage cabinet. Seems to stick fine using two-part 5-minute epoxy adhesive.

One other nit is that the volume control knob is very easy to adjust. I'd like it to have a bit more resistance so it stays at a set volume.

Also, it's not smart enough to ignore weekends. I use it as a clock radio alarm. My other clock radio knows not to go off on Saturday and Sunday. This one I have to un-alarm so it doesn't go off on weekends, and I have to remember to re-alarm it for Monday.

Still, audio quality is great and AM reception is very good.
text_fidelity_b: Sangean PR-D7 BK AM/FM Digital Rechargeable Portable Radio - Black (PR-D7BK)

text_fidelity_a:
GolfBuddy GB-WT3 Golf GPS/Rangefinder Watch Black To answer the first obvious question, yes, it can be worn comfortably on even fairly thin man's wrists. And it looks surprisingly good for something with these features. It does look like a quality object and - although a little bulky - I don't think it will bother anyone used to wearing men's wristwatches. I'm still trying to decide if the fact that it says "Golf Buddy" on it is silly, but I guess not for someone into golf and showing off their toys.

Unfortunately, you cannot get full layouts of courses with this watch, nor can you study any aspects of the course until you are there. But it does give you some very pertinent information while on the fairway or the green. But this is the tradeoff between this and a big golf GPS - you get a more convenient, less cumbersome, and less likely to annoy your friends because you're pulling it out to play with it when you should be putting device, but without the full color maps, weather and other junk you could replicate on your cell phone. And actually, I think it's a pretty nice compromise - you don't want to get so engrossed in electronics while you're out enjoying nature and weather and sport.

I also really like that it can do some basic watch and pedometer features like stopwatch, sunup/sundown, and show you how fast you are walking/biking/riding. On the flip side, since it already has the GPS, clock, and a bunch of programming script, it seems like it should house a lot more of those features; I almost expected to have many menus to explore and new features to discover for some time, but this was not the case.

It has a crazy charging "station". These days, I prefer anything just have a micro USB port so I don't have to think about extra cables or charging devices, but that would be difficult to incorporate and retain its water resistance, so it's probably the right solution, except since it has a USB-A end anyway, it should come with a 5V rectifier (most - but not everybody - has excess of these lying around).

This is a pretty nifty device for an enthusiast of both golf and gadgets, who doesn't want to bog down the game by looking at their GPS screen all day long.
text_fidelity_b: GolfBuddy GB-WT3 Golf GPS/Rangefinder Watch Black

text_fidelity_a:
Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones ...and after 13 years of heavy use, I was curious... here's my old headphones!

I went looking, because I like them so much all this time!

A couple things.

The mesh head thing- it only stayed on a couple years. They headphones worked better without it anyhow I think. Smoother on my hair. Which has a fine texture, and is a bit frizzy- lots of fine short pieces. Sometimes the foldable joints catch in them. This happens on earrings, necklaces, other headphones and other things as well. No more on this product really. Function of having fine curly hair.

Sound has always been fantastic. I love the sound and am sad when I send a ton of cash on headphones that don't come close.

They are not a snug fit, but, are soft enough and comfy enough to wear to bed. Because of the tender fabric, it's started to deteriorate on the smooth fake leathery bits. So so soft all this time though. Really to last 13 years, NO COMPLAINTS!!!.

Not snug enough to work out in. Snug enough to casually hike or walk in. They won't just fall right off or anything.

Lightweight. Easy to make a pouch or toss them into a ziplock freezer quart bag to travel and keep them in your pack or bag more tidily.

I would agree with most reviews. I tend to consider the cables 'supple' instead of 'flimsy'-- and this is an important difference! Supple cables don't just out at awkward angles and get caught on as much stuff. You can keep your music device in your pocket and the cable stays nicely under your coat or shirt and bends where you need it to stay and likes being there rather than tugging intself back in to the shape it wants to be in like a stiffer cable.

These are one of the few products I would give 10 stars to if I could.

And I still would after 13 years!!!!!!

Oh,

Actually they still work fine too. Really. I just noticed they are really a little fiddly nowadays because I used them so much, and was wondering if they still made them.

It's a bit disturbing that amazon remembered I bought them so long ago, though. I'm starting to hope Amazon never holds a grudge against me, cause they never forget!!
text_fidelity_b: Koss 155524 UR40 Collapsible Over-Ear Headphones
